edges.description: APOBEC cytidine deaminase activity generates recurrent helical-domain E542K and E545K activating mutations in PIK3CA.
Somatic mutation and focal 3p24.1 deletion inactivate TGFBR2 growth-inhibitory signaling in squamous tumors.
Chromosomal instability generates recurrent 9p24.1 focal amplifications encompassing CD274 (PD-L1) and PDCD1LG2 (PD-L2).
Dysplastic squamous epithelial cells acquire additional genetic and epigenetic alterations that breach the basement membrane and invade cervical stroma.
Constitutive PI3K pathway activation supports malignant progression to invasive cervical squamous cell carcinoma.
Loss of TGF-beta growth restraint cooperates with PI3K/MAPK alterations in invasive HPV-associated squamous cell carcinoma.
Increased CD274/PDCD1LG2 gene dosage reinforces PD-L1/PD-L2 checkpoint expression in cytolytic T-cell-infiltrated tumors.
PD-L1-mediated suppression of anti-tumor T-cell immunity permissively supports invasive cervical tumor progression despite viral and APOBEC neoantigen load.
Invasive tumor growth and mucosal friability in the vascular cervical stroma cause spontaneous intermenstrual or postmenopausal vaginal bleeding.
Friable exophytic or invasive squamous tumor on the ectocervix bleeds upon mechanical contact during intercourse.
Necrosis and mucosal disruption of invasive cervical tumor produce serous, blood-tinged, or malodorous vaginal discharge.
Deep stromal, parametrial, and pelvic sidewall infiltration compresses or invades pelvic viscerosensory and lumbosacral nerves, producing pelvic pain.
Lymphovascular space invasion enables spread to pelvic (external iliac, internal iliac, obturator) and para-aortic lymph nodes.
Chronic or heavy vaginal hemorrhage from friable invasive cervical tumor leads to iron-deficiency and blood-loss anemia, which can become life-threatening in advanced disease.
Cigarette smoking promotes high-risk HPV persistence and progression of cervical squamous neoplasia.
HIV-induced cellular immunosuppression impairs clearance of cervical high-risk HPV infection, promoting viral persistence and malignant progression.

Persistent infection of the cervical squamous epithelium by a high-risk HPV type is the initiating event of this disease; there is no host genetic lesion at the point of initiation, so the exposure link is what marks the origin.

nodes.description: Cigarette smoking is an established risk factor for HPV persistence and cervical carcinogenesis, showing a dose-response relationship with pack-years and smoking duration and risk normalization roughly 15 years after smoking cessation. A 109-study meta-analysis found pooled RR 1.70 (95% CI 1.53-1.88) for invasive cervical cancer in current vs never smokers.

nodes.description: HPV E6 promotes ATP- and ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal degradation of p53, impairing DNA-damage checkpoints and apoptosis, while HPV E7 binds and inactivates the retinoblastoma protein (pRB), releasing E2F-driven G1/S cell-cycle progression. Combined loss of p53 and pRB removes the principal checkpoints restraining proliferation of genetically damaged squamous cells.
